title: Lesson 31 - Big Objects, External Objects Security, Event Monitoring/Audit, and Run-As Exposure
description: Given a scenario, determine the appropriate access control for data outside standard/custom objects, including Big Objects, external objects, and audit/monitoring exposure.

questions.question: A Big Object stores two years of historical transaction logs for analysts. How should access be governed?
options: Object-level permissions via profile/permission sets, since Big Objects don't support the full OWD/sharing-rule/role model
OWD to Private plus sharing rules
questions.explanation: Big Objects are optimized for large-scale query and do not support the granular OWD/sharing/role model of standard objects; you govern them with object permissions and design data partitioning. The other options assume standard-object sharing that Big Objects lack.

questions.question: An External Object surfaces data from a partner's system. Who ultimately enforces record-level access to that data?
options: The external data source's own authentication/authorization, with the internal external-object permissions gating who can query at all
A sharing rule on the external object
questions.explanation: External Objects connect to external data; the external system enforces the record-level rules, while internal profile permissions control who may query the external object at all. Internal sharing rules/OWD cannot secure externally-held data.

questions.question: Why must access to Event Monitoring logs be tightly restricted?
options: Audit logs reveal query patterns and data-access behavior that is itself sensitive exposure
questions.explanation: Event monitoring logs capture who queried what and how - exposing them reveals data-access patterns and potential vulnerabilities, so access must be limited to designated admins/analysts.
